t019: Halo is an open-source AI assistant for Android today, designed around a portable runtime for other devices in the future. Ask by voice or text, use supported phone actions, keep notes and files in Notebook and Canvas, and study from material you choose. Use a model on your phone or explicitly select your own network server or cloud provider. Glasses are optional; some workflows are still being tested.

t148: One runtime, different devices and models.
t149: Halo separates input, context, model reasoning, permissions and tool execution. Android is the first host; Linux and Windows are development targets, not released apps. The aim is to keep the assistant useful without committing to a single model or gadget.

brandPromise: Private by default. Open by design.

presenceTitle: A clear signal for what Halo is doing.
presenceIntro: The open ring is Halo's body language, and the animation set comes from the Halo graphics kit, not from a running Android session. Choose a state to see it move: the ring rests when Halo is ready, travels while it thinks, closes when a task is done, and turns apricot when Halo needs you.
presenceApproveInfo: A step is waiting for approval.
presenceNote: Design-system preview, not a verified app feature. In the app, state indicators must follow real microphone, action and permission events.

presenceAltListen: Halo's open mint ring with center dot, listening.

heroOrbCaption: Halo at rest · the open ring
missionTitle: Technology should feel like a natural extension of what you can do.
missionBody: Halo is an open-source, privacy-first personal assistant. It brings voice, vision, memory, everyday tasks, phone controls and wearables into one experience, and it runs on your device first: the cloud is something you reach for, not something you fall into.
missionPill1Body: A model can run on the phone itself, so everyday questions work without a connection and without a round trip.
missionPill2Body: The gap in the ring is room to contribute. The app, the runtime and this website are all in the open.
missionPill3Body: Nothing leaves the phone quietly. Remote models are a choice you make, provider by provider.
ringIntro: A closed ring is a boundary. Ours is open on purpose.
ringGapBody: Halo is built in the open, with room for anyone to contribute.
ringRingTitle: The ring is a halo of light.
ringRingBody: Help that surrounds you quietly, instead of a screen you stare at.
ringGradientTitle: The gradient runs device to cloud.
ringGradientBody: Bright and close at the core, softer as it reaches outward.
ringCaption: The gap rests, travels, closes and calls for you.
presenceMotionNote: Fifteen of the 21 states are animated in the brand kit. The other six are shown as stills.
layersIntro: Presence never changes because of where the answer comes from. Context and conditions ride along as badges, so the ring always means the same thing.
layer1Body: The ring and its glyph. Set by what Halo is doing, never by which model is answering.
layer2Body: Where the turn is running, or what it is using. One badge, bottom right.
layer3Body: Something you need to know or act on. One badge, bottom left, and it wins attention over context.
stateIdleInfo: The ring rests with its gap at the upper right. Nothing is running.
stateListeningInfo: The ring brightens and a dot pulses, only while the microphone is open.
stateCapturingVoiceInfo: Five bars move with your voice while Halo records what you said.
stateCapturingVisionInfo: The aperture turns while the camera is capturing, and not before.
stateThinkingInfo: The gap travels a full circle while a model works out the answer.
statePlanningInfo: A short plan is drawn up before a multi-step task starts.
stateActingInfo: Three segments advance, one for each stage of the running task.
stateActingPhoneInfo: A phone glyph shows that the step happens on the device itself.
stateSpeakingInfo: Ripples travel outward, but only while audio is actually playing.
stateStreamingTextInfo: Three lines draw on in sequence for a reply with no audio.
statePreparingContextInfo: Halo gathers the material the current question needs.
stateWaitingInfo: The ring dims and an apricot dot breathes while Halo waits.
stateApprovalRequiredInfo: An apricot arc marks a step that will not run without you.
stateSuccessInfo: The gap closes into a full ring, a check draws on, and the state holds.
stateWarningInfo: An apricot arc appears next to the glyph and stays until you look.
stateErrorInfo: Ember is the only error colour, and it always arrives with a glyph.
stateRecoveringInfo: A retry arrow can repeat one step instead of work that already finished.
stateModelLoadingInfo: A progress arc follows the real download percentage.
statePermissionMissingInfo: The ring dims and holds a lock until a permission is granted.
stateOfflineInfo: A dashed ring means no connection is available right now.
stateStoppedInfo: A stopped ring holds a square until you start something new.
